selection.policy: Screen relative visual orbits, then require reviewed component identities, a credible barycentre and an adopted mass ratio. Infrared-only magnitudes and unknown component magnitudes do not pass automatically. Hierarchical pairs require explicit scope. Existing 14 examples remain labelled exceptions where appropriate.

candidates.name: μ Cassiopeiae
candidates.review: USNO grade 2 BdH2020 relative orbit. Hipparcos I/239 AstroRef=+, MultFlag=O supplies the barycentric position and proper motion at J1991.25. Bond et al. 2020 dynamical masses, adopted parallax and systemic radial velocity; visual pair Aa–Ab (also called A–B), with no additional inner orbit modelled. Absolute astrometry retains the uncertainty of the original Hipparcos orbital solution.

candidates.name: 80 Tauri
candidates.review: USNO grade 3 Trr2019 relative orbit. Component identities are the resolved Gaia DR3 and Tycho-2 pair. Barycentre position is mass-weighted from Gaia DR3 at its actual J2016.0 epoch; distance and systemic proper motion follow Torres (2019) Table 3, rather than reusing component proper motion. Adopted masses are rounded posterior modes, not an independent high-precision absolute calibration. Systemic radial velocity remains unknown. The orbit predicts the independent Gaia separation vector within 0.015 arcsec.

candidates.name: Castor
candidates.review: USNO grade 3 CIA2022d outer orbit. Adopted subsystem masses, distance and systemic velocity/proper motion come from Stellarium 26.3. Hipparcos I/239 HIP 36850 has AstroRef=A, so the component-A orbital displacement is removed from its J1991.25 position to obtain the barycentre anchor. Gaia DR3 G=2.925 identifies B; its shared AT-HYG Gaia alias is assigned only to B. Catalogue and adopted systemic-motion uncertainties limit absolute positions.

candidates.name: Procyon
candidates.review: USNO grade 3 BdH2015. Masses, adopted 285.0 mas parallax and -4.115 km/s systemic velocity follow Bond et al. (2015). Barycentric position and proper motion come from Hipparcos I/239 HIP 37279, AstroRef='+', MultFlag='O'. The astrometric anchor retains catalogue uncertainty; the relative orbit is independently checked against USNO ephemerides.

candidates.name: β Coronae Borealis
candidates.review: USNO grade 1 Mut2010b relative orbit. Hipparcos I/239 AstroRef=+, MultFlag=O supplies the barycentric position and proper motion at J1991.25. Muterspaugh et al. 2010 Table 5 and section IV.2.3 dynamical masses and S99 parallax. Systemic RV is left unknown: the paper fits separate instrumental velocity offsets; the existing catalogue RV is a component measurement. Absolute astrometry retains the uncertainty of the original Hipparcos orbital solution.

candidates.name: 70 Ophiuchi
candidates.review: USNO grade 1 Izm2019 orbit and adopted masses 0.9/0.7 from Stellarium 26.3. Absolute astrometry is the mass-weighted Gaia DR3 component solution at J2016.0. Stellarium uses a J2000 label for essentially J2016 component data; the original reference epoch is preserved here. Median component radial velocities are adopted, with catalogue limitations.

candidates.identityReview: ORB6 prints HIP 103579, an unrelated HD 200019 star at declination +44.79 degrees. HIP 103569 has HD 199766 and coordinates matching the ORB6 source position at +04.29 degrees. Preserve the printed identifier as provenance and use HIP 103569 for future component work.

scope: Reviewed additions. Remaining candidates need identity, hierarchy, barycentre and mass-ratio review; an ORB6 quality grade alone is insufficient for absolute component positions.
